mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 0.15%, it indicates a potential tightening of monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS crosses above 0.15% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both real estate investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which positively impacts the broader economy and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during an economic expansion signals strong supply-side activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases during an expansion but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which should lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which should lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.15% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and real estate investment (RSAFS) is high, it indicates a favorable monetary policy for economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low and RSAFS is high but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an economic expansion indicates strong demand in the housing market, which should lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases during an expansion but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.
